tools.name: list_node_access_rules

List a node's access rules (IP and Origin allowlists, Global nodes only).

With no active rules, the node accepts requests from any IP and origin.
If correctly configured rules still return 403, that's a support case:
offer contact_chainstack.

tools.description:
Delete an access rule from a node (irreversible).

what's enforced afterwards. With no active rules left, the node accepts
requests from any IP and origin.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "contact_chainstack" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: contact_chainstack · Private data: contact_chainstack, get_chainstack_pricing · Public sink: contact_chainstack, request_testnet_funds · Destructive: delete_project, delete_node, update_node_access_rule, delete_node_access_rule.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: contact_chainstack · Private data: contact_chainstack, get_chainstack_pricing · Public sink: contact_chainstack, request_testnet_funds · Destructive: delete_project, delete_node, update_node_access_rule, delete_node_access_rule

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
